memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They made curtains of goat hair for the tent over the tabernacle - eleven altogether. All eleven curtains were the same size - thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. They joined five of the curtains into one set and the other six into another set. Then they made fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in one set and also along the edge of the end curtain in the other set." - Exod 36:14-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now a second layer goes on. Goat hair this time, not fine linen. Coarse, dark, weather-resistant. Eleven curtains rather than ten, so this outer layer extended further and covered more.

Nobody admired the goat hair. From outside, the tabernacle looked plain — a dark tent in the wilderness. The beauty was all inside.

There is something here about God's way of working that runs right through Scripture. Isaiah said of the coming Servant that He had no beauty or majesty to attract us to Him, nothing in His appearance that we should desire Him (Isa 53:2). Jesus came in a plain wrapping. People looked at Him and saw a carpenter from Nazareth.

The same principle applies to the church, and to us. God has chosen the foolish things of the world to shame the wise, the weak things to shame the strong (1 Cor 1:27). What He is building rarely looks impressive from outside.

Do not judge a life, a church, or a season by its outer covering. The glory is usually inside.

And do not despair if your own life feels like goat hair rather than fine linen. The plain layer was doing exactly what God commanded — protecting everything precious underneath.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you judge people or churches by outward impressiveness?
2. Does your life feel plain to you? What might God be protecting through it?
3. Where has God's beauty been hidden inside something ordinary in your experience?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me see past appearances. Thank You that You work through what looks plain and unimpressive. Amen.
